readiness_assessment.reasoning: Horse domestication section is well-supported archaeologically (Botai 3-evidence convergence) and genetically (Western steppe expansion documented). However, unresolved debate over domestication origins (single vs. multiple events) must be transparent in narration. Faz C red-team flags correctly identify nuances: Botai is 'oldest known' not 'sole origin'; replacement was incomplete (introgression occurred). These do not block production but require explicit caveats.
qualifications: C-B1-001: 'Horse domestication occurred at Botai' should state: 'Earliest known evidence of horse domestication is at Botai culture (~3500 BCE); whether this was the sole domestication center or one of multiple independent events remains debated by archaeologists and geneticists'

C-B1-003: 'Western steppe horses spread globally' should include: 'Western steppe horses became genetically dominant by 2000 BCE, though some regions show evidence of local wild-horse populations persisting or interbreeding rather than complete replacement'

audit_findings.note: 3/3 core claims linked to Nature publication + archaeological reports; high-quality sources
Metrical analysis, pathological markers, organic residue chemistry — all primary evidence; Botai excavations are direct material culture
Botai evidence supported by Nature (2021) + Nature-adjacent publications; genetic evidence from multiple labs
Faz C found and documented: alternative domestication sites, genetic discontinuity arguments, regional variation in replacement patterns; none invalidate Botai timing but complicate origin narrative
CLAIM_MUTATION_SUSPECTED (C-B1-003) and FALSE_PRECISION (C-B1-001) flags documented; D2 qualifications address these in production language
Three competing schools documented: Botai-focused, Western steppe consensus, Multiple domestication hypothesis; not single-perspective

research_gaps.question: Genetic continuity between Botai (3500 BCE) and Western steppe horses (2000 BCE) — same lineage or independent origins?
research_gaps.evidence_potential: Ancient DNA from Botai and Western steppe comparative analysis could resolve; studies are ongoing

production_requirements: Narration must distinguish 'earliest known site' (Botai) from 'sole origin' (unproven)
Must acknowledge ongoing geneticist debate on single vs. multiple domestication
Western steppe dominance is established; regional variation (introgression vs. replacement) should be noted if space permits
